info.title: Luminarity Shouldcosting API
info.description: API for CAD geometry mining by Luminarity (shouldcosting.com). Uploads CAD files (base64-encoded), queues them for geometry analysis (mining), polls progress, and retrieves structured results including manufacturing parameters (volumes, surfaces, bores, material groups, bounding boxes) and 2D/3D previews. IMPORTANT: This API does NOT return prices or costs — it returns the ~47 geometry/manufacturing parameters per component that serve as inputs to a cost model. The actual price calculation must be done client-side. The API server runs on Kestrel (.NET). Authentication is via the customerID field in request bodies. All response field names use camelCase.
info.x-tested-on: 2026-02-19 - Live endpoint testing with 8 real STEP files + 5 unsupported format tests (2 PDF, 3 IPT). STEP files: block.stp (10K/molding), 4pinplug.stp (57K/assembly/7parts), Pump Manifold v3.step (493K/turning), eMG1-110-G4.stp (590K/assembly/8parts), boxy_with_cylindricity.stp (85K/milling/threads), boxy_with_diamsize.stp (86K/milling), io1-ac-214.stp (50K/turning/AP214), io1-ca-214.stp (108K/turning/AP214). Unsupported formats tested: 2D PDF drawings (Welle.pdf, Abschaltung Pneumatik.pdf) → INVALID_DATATYPE; Autodesk Inventor IPT (Scheibe.ipt, Kettenrad.ipt, Grundkörper.ipt) → INVALID_DATATYPE. All 9 endpoints verified, 4 material groups observed (molding/milling/turning/assembly).

x-supported-formats.rejection_behavior: Files with unsupported extensions are accepted by POST /api/costchecker (returns IN_QUEUE), but the cadminer immediately sets miningStatus=INVALID_DATATYPE with no preview, no miningResult, and null miningDuration. The costchecker lightweight status endpoint may continue to show IN_QUEUE even after rejection — always use GET /api/cadminer/{fileName} for authoritative status.
x-supported-formats.note: The API only accepts 3D CAD exchange formats (STEP/STP). Proprietary native formats (Autodesk Inventor .ipt, SolidWorks .sldprt, etc.) and 2D formats (.pdf, .dxf, .dwg) are NOT supported. Files must be exported to STEP format before upload. Other potentially supported formats (IGES .igs/.iges, Parasolid .x_t/.x_b, JT .jt) have not been tested.

x-workflow.description: Single-step CAD geometry mining workflow. The API performs geometry analysis (volumes, surfaces, bores, material group classification) — NOT price calculation. The mining results provide manufacturing parameters that must be fed into your own cost model to derive prices.
x-workflow.x-important-clarification: Despite the 'costchecker' naming, this API does NOT return prices or costs. It returns CAD geometry mining data (47+ fields per component) including material_group, volumes, surfaces, bore counts, bounding boxes, thread indicators, etc. These are INPUTS to a cost formula. The actual should-costing (price derivation) must happen on the client side or in a separate system. The cmxml config file on the server controls which geometry features are extracted.
x-workflow.x-single-step-confirmed: Verified from original PDF documentation (22.09.25, 9 pages, German) and live API testing (2026-02-19). There is NO two-step process. The upload (POST /api/costchecker) triggers both queuing AND mining in one step. There is no second POST needed to trigger cost calculation after mining completes. The '/api/costchecker/miningresult' endpoint is simply a JSON-formatted view of the same mining data available as CSV in the CADminerEntry.miningResult field.
steps: 1. UPLOAD: POST /api/costchecker — Submit CAD file (base64) with customerID, cmXml, fileExtension. Returns filenameServer GUID immediately. Mining starts automatically.
2. POLL STATUS: GET /api/costchecker/{filenameServer} — Lightweight (~200 bytes). Check status field: IN_QUEUE → MINING → DONE (or ERROR/INVALID_DATATYPE/BLACKLISTED). Poll every 2-5 seconds.
3. POLL PROGRESS (optional): GET /api/cadminer/progress/{fileName} — Detailed BOM progress for assemblies (e.g. 'Component 2/15'). Useful for progress bars.
4. FETCH RESULTS (when DONE): Two equivalent options for the same data:
4a. GET /api/costchecker/miningresult/{filenameServer} — Structured JSON with csv_data array of objects (RECOMMENDED for programmatic use)
4b. GET /api/cadminer/{fileName} — Full CADminerEntry with miningResult as semicolon-separated CSV string, PLUS base64 preview PNG (WARNING: 150-250KB+ response)
5. PREVIEW IMAGES: Available via base64 in CADminerEntry.preview, OR via static file server at http://95.156.230.220/{guid-without-ext}.png (lighter alternative)
6. QUEUE MONITORING (optional): GET /api/cadminer/queue and /api/cadminer/queue/count for dashboard displays

resultFormats.csvFormat: CADminerEntry.miningResult — semicolon-separated key=value pairs (e.g. 'master_material_group=molding;pd_volume=60;...'). For assemblies: multiple lines separated by \r\n, first line = aggregated, subsequent lines = per-component.
resultFormats.jsonFormat: MiningResult via /api/costchecker/miningresult — { result: [{ csv_data: [{field: value, ...}] }], status: 'DONE' }. Same data as CSV but structured. For assemblies: csv_data array has one object per component.

x-workflow.authentication: Authentication is embedded in the request body via the customerID field (tenant API key). No HTTP auth headers required. GET endpoints for status/progress/queue do not require authentication.
x-workflow.errorHandling: Errors return either: (1) CostCheckerResult with null identifiers and status='ERROR ...' for business logic errors, or (2) ASP.NET ProblemDetails (application/problem+json) for framework-level errors (404, malformed JSON).

x-naming-explanation.costchecker: Namespace for upload (POST) and result retrieval (GET miningresult). Named 'costchecker' because the geometry mining data feeds into cost estimation — but the API itself does NOT calculate costs.
x-naming-explanation.cadminer: Namespace for status polling (GET entry), progress tracking (GET progress), and queue management. The actual geometry analysis engine.

servers.description: Static file server for preview images (.png), STL models (.stl), and ZIP archives (.zip). File paths: /{filenameServer-without-ext}.{png|stl|zip}

post.summary: Upload a CAD file for geometry mining
post.description: Uploads a CAD file (base64-encoded) for geometry mining. This is a SINGLE-STEP process: the file is queued and mining starts automatically — no second POST is needed. Returns a `filenameServer` GUID which is the key for all subsequent polling and result retrieval. Authentication is via the `customerID` field in the body. The `cmXml` field references a server-side .cmxml config controlling which geometry features are extracted (e.g. 'luminarity_rsa'). The cmxml can enable assembly analysis via <Assemblies>true</Assemblies>. On validation errors, returns CostCheckerResult with null identifiers and error description in `status`.

200.description: File accepted and queued for mining. The `filenameServer` field contains the GUID-based server filename used for all subsequent API calls.

400.description: Validation error. Returns the CostCheckerResult schema with null identifiers and an error message in the `status` field. Common errors: 'ERROR Empty modelFile3D' (missing file data), 'ERROR Unknown CustomerID' (invalid customerID), 'ERROR Invalid or missing cmxml definition: {path}' (bad cmXml reference).

For authoritative mining status, always use GET /api/cadminer/{fileName} instead. This endpoint is best used only for lightweight polling during active MINING.

post.description: Creates a new CADminer entry in the database. This is an internal/administrative endpoint used by the system to register files. The request body must conform to the CADminerEntry schema. Returns 405 Method Not Allowed for GET requests. Verified via live testing: GET returns 405 with Allow: POST.

400.description: Invalid request body or validation error. May return ASP.NET ProblemDetails for JSON parsing errors, or a stack trace for database constraint violations (e.g. UNIQUE constraint on FileName).

405.description: Method not allowed. Only POST is supported on this path (GET is not available; use GET /api/cadminer/{fileName} instead).

500.description: Server error (e.g. database constraint violation on duplicate fileName).

get.summary: Poll mining progress for a file
get.description: Returns progress information for a mining job directly as a ProgressDetail object (not wrapped). Includes BOM component progress, current step number, and a human-readable progress text. Returns the progress even for files with issues (e.g. progressText='INVALID_CONTENT'). Note: the path uses a path parameter, NOT a query parameter. The endpoint also supports PUT method. Verified via live testing.

get.description: Returns the structured mining result for a completed analysis as JSON. This is the SAME data as the semicolon-separated CSV in CADminerEntry.miningResult, but formatted as a JSON array of objects. Only available when miningStatus=DONE. Returns 404 for files still mining or with non-DONE status. Contains ~47 geometry/manufacturing parameters per component (volumes, surfaces, bores, material groups, bounding boxes, thread indicators) — NOT prices or costs. Verified via live testing: returns 404 for non-DONE files.

CadFile.description: Request body for uploading a CAD file for geometry mining. Field names are case-insensitive on input (both camelCase and PascalCase accepted). The customerID field serves as the authentication token (tenant API key). The cmXml field references a .cmxml calculation config on the server (filename without extension).

cmXml.description: References a calculation configuration (.cmxml) file on the server within the tenant's directory. This determines the cost calculation parameters used during mining. Must match an existing configuration file name (without extension).

customerID.description: Tenant-specific API key that serves as both authentication and customer identification. Format: 'lum-{hash}-{tenant}'. This determines which tenant directory is used on the server for configuration files.

fileExtension.description: File extension including the leading dot. Supported formats include STEP (.stp, .step), STL (.stl), and other CAD formats.

file.description: Base64-encoded content of the CAD file.

CostCheckerResult.description: Response returned after uploading a CAD file (POST /api/costchecker) or querying file status (GET /api/costchecker/{filenameServer}). On success, contains the GUID-based server filename. On error (400), identifiers are null and the status field contains the error description. All field names are camelCase. FRONTEND NOTE: This is a lightweight response (~200 bytes) suitable for frequent polling. Use GET /api/costchecker/{filenameServer} for status checks before fetching the heavy CADminerEntry. Verified via live testing.

x-frontend-notes.pollingUse: Use this lightweight endpoint for status polling. Only fetch CADminerEntry when you need preview data.
x-frontend-notes.errorDetection: Check if filenameServer is null to detect errors. The status field will contain the error message starting with 'ERROR'.
x-frontend-notes.statusField: The status field contains EITHER a MiningStatusEnum value (IN_QUEUE, MINING, DONE, etc.) OR a free-text error string starting with 'ERROR'. Parse accordingly.

filenameServer.description: Server-assigned filename in GUID+extension format (e.g. 'b1ebfed3-e0e6-4397-b22a-e42a30426afd.stp'). This is the primary key used to track the file through all subsequent API calls. Null on validation errors.

fileID.description: SHA256 hash of the uploaded file content (uppercase hex), used for deduplication. Null on validation errors.

status.description: Current status. On success: a MiningStatusEnum value (e.g. 'IN_QUEUE'). On error: a descriptive string starting with 'ERROR' (e.g. 'ERROR Unknown CustomerID', 'ERROR Empty modelFile3D').

cadMinerResult.description: Mining results summary in semicolon-separated key=value format (same format as CADminerEntry.miningResult). Null when first queued, empty string during mining, populated with results when DONE. Decimal values use comma as separator (European locale). For assemblies, components separated by \r\n.

CADminerEntry.description: Complete mining entry for a file returned by GET /api/cadminer/{fileName}. Includes status, previews (base64-encoded), and metadata. All field names are camelCase except the unusual 'shA256'. IMPORTANT FOR FRONTEND: The response can be very large (200KB+) due to the base64-encoded preview PNG which alone can be ~163K characters. The preview is available as soon as miningStatus transitions from IN_QUEUE to MINING, even before mining completes. The preview3D (STL) may only appear after mining is DONE. For lighter polling, use GET /api/costchecker/{filenameServer} (small response) or GET /api/cadminer/progress/{fileName} (progress only). Alternatively, preview images are available as static files at http://95.156.230.220/{guid-without-ext}.png to avoid large base64 payloads. Verified field names via live testing.

x-frontend-notes.responseSize: Typical response is 150-250KB due to base64 preview data. Plan for large payloads.
x-frontend-notes.previewRendering: Decode the preview field (base64 PNG) using: const img = new Image(); img.src = 'data:image/png;base64,' + response.preview; Alternatively, use the static file URL: http://95.156.230.220/{guid-without-ext}.png
x-frontend-notes.preview3DRendering: The preview3D field contains base64-encoded STL data. Use a Three.js STLLoader or similar to render: const blob = new Blob([Uint8Array.from(atob(response.preview3D), c => c.charCodeAt(0))]); Alternatively, use the static file URL: http://95.156.230.220/{guid-without-ext}.stl
x-frontend-notes.pollingStrategy: 1. Upload via POST /api/costchecker -> get filenameServer. 2. Poll GET /api/cadminer/progress/{fileName} for real-time progress. 3. Poll GET /api/costchecker/{filenameServer} for lightweight status checks. 4. When status=DONE, fetch full entry via GET /api/cadminer/{fileName} for previews. 5. Get structured results via GET /api/costchecker/miningresult/{filenameServer}.
x-frontend-notes.statusTransitions: IN_QUEUE -> MINING -> DONE (success) or INVALID_DATATYPE/ERROR/BLACKLISTED (failure). Preview PNG becomes available during MINING phase.
x-frontend-notes.observedPreviewSize: 163,480 characters of base64 (~122KB decoded PNG) for a simple single-component STEP file. Assemblies with many components will likely produce larger previews.

fileName.description: Server-assigned filename in GUID+extension format (same as filenameServer from CostCheckerResult). Use this as the key for all subsequent API calls.

shA256.description: SHA256 hash of the uploaded file content (uppercase hex). Note the unusual camelCase serialization: 'shA256' (not 'sha256' or 'SHA256'). This matches the fileID field in CostCheckerResult.

cmXml.description: Full server-side Windows path to the .cmxml calculation configuration file used for this mining job. This is an internal server path and should NOT be displayed to end users.

miningResult.description: Mining result as a semicolon-separated key=value string (NOT JSON). Decimal values use COMMA as separator (European locale, e.g. '1,67' = 1.67). Empty string while mining is in progress or on error. For assemblies, components are separated by \r\n. FRONTEND NOTE: For structured/typed data, prefer using GET /api/costchecker/miningresult/{filenameServer} which returns proper JSON with period decimals.

preview.description: Base64-encoded PNG preview image of the CAD model. FRONTEND NOTE: This field can be very large (observed: 163,480 chars / ~122KB decoded for a simple part). Available as soon as miningStatus='MINING'. Empty string ('') if no preview could be generated (e.g. INVALID_DATATYPE files). To render: set img.src = 'data:image/png;base64,' + this_value. For lighter payloads, use the static file URL instead: http://95.156.230.220/{guid-without-ext}.png. The PNG dimensions observed: 714x510 pixels (from base64 header 'AAAsoAAAH+CA').

preview3D.description: Base64-encoded STL 3D model data. Null when not yet generated (during MINING) or unavailable. To render in frontend: decode base64, create Blob, load with Three.js STLLoader. Static file alternative: http://95.156.230.220/{guid-without-ext}.stl. Assembly components use naming: {masterGuid}_{componentName}.stl

customerID.description: The tenant API key used when the file was uploaded. This is the same value passed as customerID in the upload request.

language.description: Language code for localized mining results. Null if not set during upload. Supported values: de, en, fr, it, es, pt.

miningDateTime.description: ISO 8601 timestamp WITHOUT timezone (local server time) of when the mining process completed or when a terminal status was set (e.g. INVALID_DATATYPE). Null while file is still IN_QUEUE or MINING. Format observed: '2026-02-19T16:49:11' (no Z suffix, no timezone offset).

miningDuration.description: Duration of the mining process in seconds with comma as decimal separator (European locale). Null if mining has not completed. FRONTEND NOTE: Replace comma with period before parsing as float: parseFloat(value.replace(',', '.')). Observed values: '2,5004669' (2.5s for block.stp), '6,3885687' (6.4s for 4pinplug.stp), '14,9884518' (15s for Pump Manifold), '36,4456429' (36.4s for eMG1).

ProgressDetail.description: Mining progress information returned directly by GET /api/cadminer/progress/{fileName}. Note: this is returned as a flat JSON object, NOT wrapped in any envelope. All field names are camelCase. FRONTEND NOTE: Use this for progress bars and status indicators. The bomProgress field gives 'current/total' BOM components (e.g. '2/15'). Use progressValue/progressMax for a percentage-based progress bar. The progressText field provides human-readable status. A progressText of 'INVALID_CONTENT' indicates the file has content issues. Verified via live testing.

x-frontend-notes.progressBar: Calculate percentage: (progressValue / progressMax) * 100. Handle progressMax=0 as indeterminate.
x-frontend-notes.bomDisplay: Parse bomProgress string (e.g. '2/15') to show 'Processing component 2 of 15'.
x-frontend-notes.errorState: If progressText contains 'INVALID', display a warning to the user.

bomProgress.description: Bill of Materials progress in 'current/total' format (e.g. '2/15'). Empty string if BOM information is not available.

progressMax.description: Total number of progress steps. 0 if total is unknown.

component.description: Name of the BOM component currently being processed. Empty string if not applicable.

progressText.description: Human-readable progress description. May contain status indicators like 'INVALID_CONTENT' for problematic files.

MiningStatusEnum.description: Status of the mining process for a CAD file. Verified values via live testing: IN_QUEUE (just uploaded), MINING (being processed), INVALID_DATATYPE (file format not recognized), DONE (results available).

MiningResult.description: Structured mining result returned by GET /api/costchecker/miningresult/{filenameServer} when miningStatus=DONE. NOTE: The Content-Type returned by the server is 'text/plain' despite being valid JSON. Contains detailed CAD analysis including material classification, dimensions, volumes, bore information, and processing time. For assemblies, csv_data contains multiple entries (one per component). Verified via live testing with 4 real STEP files.

x-frontend-notes.contentType: Server returns Content-Type: text/plain, but the body is valid JSON. Parse with JSON.parse().
x-frontend-notes.assemblyHandling: For assemblies (master_material_group='assembly'), csv_data contains multiple objects. Components without CAD data appear as { master_cad_file_name: 'Component1 (keine CAD-Datei)' } with no other fields.
x-frontend-notes.materialGroups: Observed master_material_group values: 'molding' (simple solid parts, e.g. block.stp), 'milling' (prismatic parts with bores/threads, e.g. boxy_with_cylindricity.stp), 'turning' (rotational/lathe parts with profile data, e.g. Pump Manifold, io1-*.stp), 'assembly' (multi-component assemblies, e.g. 4pinplug.stp, eMG1-110-G4.stp).
x-frontend-notes.negativeValues: A value of -1 indicates 'not applicable' or 'not detected' for that measurement.
x-frontend-notes.units: Dimensions appear to be in mm. Volumes in mm^3. Areas in mm^2. Processing time in milliseconds (Zeit(ms) field).
x-frontend-notes.profileData: master_cad_profile_start/end contain pipe-separated profile descriptions (e.g. 'E|114.3$Z|114.3|9.53$E|114.3'). master_cad_characteristic shows shape sequence (e.g. 'E$Z$E$Z$SF$Z$SF$E$Ko$SF$Ra$SF$E').

result.description: Array containing a single result object with csv_data.

csv_data.description: Array of component analysis objects. Each object contains ~40+ key-value pairs with manufacturing analysis data. For single parts, this array has one element. For assemblies, it has one element per component (first is the master, subsequent are individual components). Components without CAD data may only have master_cad_file_name.

status.description: Overall status of the mining result. Value is 'DONE' when results are available.

MiningResultEntry.description: Individual component analysis from a mining result. Contains ~40+ fields covering material classification, geometry measurements, bore/thread detection, and processing time. All numeric fields use period as decimal separator in the JSON response (note: the CADminerEntry.miningResult semicolon-separated format uses comma as decimal separator). A value of -1 typically means 'not applicable' or 'not detected'. Verified field names and types via live testing with block.stp, 4pinplug.stp, Pump Manifold v3.step, and eMG1-110-G4.stp.

master_cad_file_name.description: The server-side GUID (without extension) for the analyzed file, or a component description for assembly sub-parts (e.g. 'Component1 (keine CAD-Datei)' for components without individual CAD files).

master_material_group.description: Detected material/manufacturing group classification. Observed values from live testing: 'molding' (simple solid parts, e.g. block.stp), 'milling' (prismatic parts with bores/threads, e.g. boxy_with_cylindricity.stp), 'turning' (rotational/lathe parts with profile, e.g. Pump Manifold, io1-*.stp), 'assembly' (multi-component assemblies, e.g. 4pinplug.stp, eMG1-110-G4.stp).

master_material_group_hit_rate.description: Confidence of material group classification. -1 means not applicable.

pd_isc_surfaces.description: ISC (Important Surface Characteristics) surface area in mm^2.

number_of_parts_in_assembly.description: Number of components in an assembly. 0 for single parts.

pd_surface_full_part.description: Total surface area of the part in mm^2.

pd_cutting_volume.description: Material to be removed by cutting in mm^3.

pd_total_inner_loop.description: Total inner loop length. -1 if not applicable.

master_total_length_inner_loop.description: Total length of inner loops in mm. -1 if not applicable.

master_total_length_outer_loop.description: Total length of outer loops in mm. -1 if not applicable.

pd_total_length_all_loops.description: Total length of all loops in mm. -1 if not applicable.

pd_num_bends.description: Number of bends detected. -1 if not applicable.

pd_number_of_threads_from_table.description: Number of threads detected from thread table.

pd_number_of_threads_from_surface.description: Number of threads detected from surface analysis.

pd_number_of_threads_from_curves.description: Number of threads detected from curve analysis.

master_thread_diameter.description: Thread diameter in mm. 0 or -1 if no threads.

master_min_diameter.description: Minimum outer diameter in mm. -1 if not applicable. Can also be -2000 indicating a detection anomaly (observed with io1-ac-214.stp AP214 format). For turning parts: typically the smallest outer profile diameter.

master_max_diameter.description: Maximum outer diameter in mm. -1 if not applicable. Can also be -2000 indicating a detection anomaly. For turning parts: typically the largest outer profile diameter (e.g. 114.3 for Pump Manifold, 88 for io1-ca-214).

master_min_diameter_inner.description: Minimum inner diameter in mm. -1 if not applicable.

master_max_diameter_inner.description: Maximum inner diameter in mm. -1 if not applicable.

master_cad_profile_start.description: CAD profile start description. Either -1 (not applicable) or a pipe/dollar-separated string describing the profile geometry (e.g. 'E|114.3$Z|114.3|9.53$E|114.3').

master_cad_profile_end.description: CAD profile end description. Either -1 (not applicable) or a pipe/dollar-separated string.

master_shape_maxlenght_between_start_end.description: Maximum length between profile start and end in mm. -1 if not applicable. Note: field name contains typo 'maxlenght' (not 'maxlength').

master_cad_characteristic.description: CAD shape characteristic sequence. Either -1 (not applicable) or a dollar-separated string of shape codes (e.g. 'E$Z$E$Z$SF$Z$SF$E$Ko$SF$Ra$SF$E').

master_number_of_sections.description: Number of profile sections. -1 if not applicable.

master_bore_collection.description: Bore collection data. Either -1 (not applicable) or a pipe/dollar-separated string describing detected bores. Format per bore: '{index}|{type}|{count}|{diameter}|{depth}[|{thread}]'. Bore types observed: 'd' (drilled bore), 'g' (ground/groove bore). Thread suffix: '|th6' indicates M6 thread. Examples from live testing: '1|d|6|6.76|9.53$2|d|6|9.52|0' (Pump Manifold - 3 bore groups), '1|d|2|5|10|th6$7|g|10|5|10.5' (boxy parts - threaded and ground bores).

master_number_of_keyway.description: Number of keyways detected. Only present in some responses.

master_type_of_keyway_open.description: Number of open keyways. Only present in some responses.

master_type_of_keyway_closed.description: Number of closed keyways. Only present in some responses.

master_element_keyway.description: Keyway element data. -1 if not applicable. Present in newer responses instead of master_number_of_keyway/master_type_of_keyway_open/master_type_of_keyway_closed.

Zeit(ms).description: Processing time in milliseconds for this component's analysis.

ProblemDetails.description: Standard ASP.NET Core ProblemDetails response for HTTP errors (RFC 7807). Returned by the framework for 404, 400 validation errors, and other HTTP errors. Verified via live testing.

type.description: URI reference identifying the problem type (RFC link).

title.description: Short human-readable summary of the problem.

errors.description: Detailed validation errors (only present for 400 validation responses).
